findings.claim: The three-measure size comparison names a four-word clause as its object, but the measures hold only for the whole verse; as written the claim is false on all three measures and its shorter-only-against-115:6-115:7 rider is false too.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale (repeated verbatim in observed_substrate_signals[0]) reads: 135:17's own clause (oshb:Ps.135.17: אָזְנַ֣יִם לָ֭הֶם וְלֹ֣א יַאֲזִ֑ינוּ) is longer than 115:6 alone on all 3 measures taken (skeleton words, consonants, codepoints), running shorter only against 115:6-115:7 combined. Re-measured from verse_map_oshb.json (skeleton tier for words and consonants, raw codepoints for the third): the quoted clause = 4 skeleton words / 17 consonants / 36 codepoints; MT 115:6 whole = 8 / 30 / 67; MT 115:6-115:7 combined = 17 / 70 / 156. The clause is therefore SHORTER than MT 115:6 on all three measures, and shorter than the combined pair as well. The stated relation holds only when the object is MT 135:17 as a WHOLE VERSE (9 / 32 / 70), longer than MT 115:6 on all three and shorter than 115:6-115:7 combined. Not load-bearing: the row itself rules the Ps 115 material discussion texture (discussed here as a recognizable, recurring cross-psalm texture, not merged with Ps 115's own rows), and both seams rest elsewhere -- the 135:14|15 edge on the fresh idol topic opening at oshb:Ps.135.15 against the prefix-conjugation hinge couplet of MT 135:13-14 (byte-checked: MT 135:8 and MT 135:10 do both open with a relative-plus-suffix-conjugation form, as the row says), and the 135:18|19 edge on the imperative bless-call at MT 135:19. Cross-row coherent: M8-Ps-445 and M8-Ps-447 argue the same two seams the same way.
findings.proposed_change: Rename the count object to the whole verse: MT 135:17 as a whole verse runs longer than MT 115:6 (9 vs 8 skeleton words, 32 vs 30 consonants, 70 vs 67 codepoints) and shorter than MT 115:6-115:7 combined (17 / 70 / 156); retain the four-word splice only as the identification of the clause the two verses share.

findings.claim: Naming only six finite-verb-headed verses as the interruption of the participial run implies far more participial heads across 136:4-25 than the bytes carry.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative both say the participial construction recurs through 136:4-25 but is interrupted by six finite-verb-headed verses (136:11,14,15,18,21,24). The digit re-derives TRUE: exactly six of the 22 verses in MT 136:4-25 are headed by a finite verb (136:11 וַיּוֹצֵ֣א, 136:14, 136:15, 136:18, 136:21, 136:24). But the lamed-participle head covers only 9 of those 22 verses (136:4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 13, 16, 17, plus the bare participle at 136:25); the remaining seven are headed by the object marker (136:8 and 136:9, אֶת), a prepositional phrase (136:12), lamed plus a proper name (136:19 לְ֭סִיחוֹן and 136:20), a bare noun (136:22 נַ֭חֲלָה) and a relative particle (136:23). Not load-bearing: the 136:3|4 seam rests on the byte-true form change from the imperative הוֹד֣וּ (oshb:Ps.136.1) heading MT 136:1-3 to the lamed-participle לְעֹ֘שֵׂ֤ה (oshb:Ps.136.4), and the next row argues that same seam on the same footing while itself noting the object-marker heads at 136:8-9.
findings.proposed_change: Scope the claim: a participial construction that heads 9 of the 22 verses in 136:4-25 (136:4-7, 10, 13, 16, 17, 25), interrupted by six finite-verb-headed verses (136:11, 14, 15, 18, 21, 24) and by object-marker, prepositional, proper-name, nominal and relative heads elsewhere.

triggers.grounds: The medium_low band itself is defensible and both seams are sound at byte tier: MT 141:4 is petition (negative jussive) and MT 141:5 turns to third-person description, while MT 141:8 reopens direct address with the vocative יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ps.141.8) -- a vocative opening, which the book's row-granularity rule treats as a tier-1 internal seam -- and the row's claim that no vocative Yahweh occurs within vv5-7 while it is present in vv1, 3 and again at v8 re-derives TRUE from the bytes of MT 141:1-8. What does NOT survive is the STATED REASON for the band and the row's evidence base. The reason is located in the translation (the connective logic across these three verses remains genuinely unsettled in the WEB rendering itself), and the substrate-signal list adds a WEB quotation-mark fact (web:Ps.141.7 is rendered as quoted speech in WEB with no marked speaker); both are tier-4 metadata, which is never boundary evidence and never a confidence ground. The obscurity sits in MT's own syntax -- כִּי ע֥וֹד וּ֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ps.141.5) and נִשְׁמְט֣וּ בִֽידֵי סֶ֭לַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Ps.141.6) -- and the row cites no oshb: ref and splices no Hebrew anywhere, so its low-band warrant cannot be checked at byte tier from the row itself. Ps 141 is a titled identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json), so the WEB refs resolve and no title ref is owed by a non-opening row; the span crosses no K/Q (pmarks_Ps.json lists none in Ps 141) and no selah. Band: keep medium_low. Stated reason and evidence base: defective.

findings.claim: The book-wide saints-term digit (26 verses) counts a consonantal substring, not the two spellings the sentence names; the named object occurs in 10 verses, and the 26 includes a different lexeme.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals[3] and device_notes all read: the saints-term (chasidim/chasidav) recurring at 149:1, 149:5, and 149:9 (3 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier). Re-swept at skeleton tier over the MT verse map: the contiguous consonantal substring chet-samekh-yod-dalet occurs in exactly 26 verses -- that is where the digit comes from -- but the two spellings the sentence NAMES, חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5) and חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9), occur in only 10 verses book-wide (2 and 8 respectively). The 16-verse remainder is other forms (MT 4:4, 12:2, 16:10, 18:26, 32:6, 43:1, 50:5, 52:11, 79:2, 86:2, 89:20, 104:17, 132:9, 132:16, 145:10, 145:17), and MT 104:17's member is חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה -- the stork, a different lexeme -- exactly the contained-substring trap the book's sweep hazard catalog names. The load-bearing half of the sentence, 3 of 3 Psalm 149 members, is byte-TRUE and is what keeps the whole_psalm rival live at medium confidence, so the defective digit is not alone load-bearing. The same sentence is carried on the paired row for 149:5-9 (there as 2 of 3 members; 26 verses book-wide), so any cure is a seam-pair cure installed on both.
findings.proposed_change: Either rename the object to match the digit (the saints-root chet-samekh-yod-dalet as a consonantal substring: 26 verses book-wide, skeleton tier, including the homographic stork at MT 104:17) or keep the named spellings and correct the digit to 10 verses book-wide; install the same wording on the paired 149:5-9 row.
